A .jot is plain text, but the tasks, events and numbers in it can be read by a program. This guide covers what you can do with them: put your events on your calendar, bring in numbers from a fitness app, carry unfinished tasks forward, and connect to other services.

What gets sent, and when. Nothing in Jot reaches the internet unless you run something that says it will, or turn on a setting that says it will. The workspace's tools work entirely in your browser. Whatever comes back from a service is written into your journal as an ordinary record, marked with source:, so the .jot file stays the master copy.

In the workspace: the Tools row

Above the writing, in Write:

Tool What it does
Today ＋ adds today's dated entry, if there is none, and puts the cursor in it
Carry tasks forward → open tasks from earlier days are marked [>] (moved) where they were, and written again under today
Week review adds a review of this week: how many tasks were done, which are still open, each number's average, a chart and two questions
Calendar .ics ↓ your events and dated tasks as a calendar file: import it into Google Calendar, Apple Calendar, Outlook …
Numbers .csv ↓ · Tasks .csv ↓ the numbers (date, metric, value, unit) or the tasks, for a spreadsheet
Import numbers ↥ numbers from a CSV (a health or fitness app's export) written into their days

A tool that changes your writing does it in one step, so Ctrl+Z (Cmd+Z on a Mac) takes it back.

Events and tasks on your calendar

The calendar file has:

  • Events (lines starting o ). If the line has a time (19:00, 7:30pm, at 21) the event is an hour long at that time; otherwise it lasts all day. A bare "at 7" is not a time: morning or evening? Write 7pm or 19:00.
  • Tasks that are open ([ ], [!]) on a dated day, as to-dos due that day. Done, moved and cancelled tasks are left out.
### 2026-10-28 | Wednesday

o Dentist 09:30
o Market, all day
[ ] Post the letter

Each event and task keeps the same identity in every export, so importing a newer file updates entries instead of adding them twice. Google Calendar shows events but not to-dos: in VS Code, turn on jot.automation.calendar.tasksAsEvents to put tasks in as all-day events too.

Numbers from a fitness or health app

Most apps (Google Fit, Garmin, Fitbit, sleep and step counters, a spreadsheet) can export a CSV. Jot needs one column of dates and columns of numbers; the column names become the metrics, and a unit in brackets is kept (Sleep (h) becomes metric sleep, unit h):

Date,Steps,Sleep (h)
2026-10-26,8200,7.5
2026-10-27,6400,6.75
  • Each number goes into its day. If your template has an empty value: for that metric on that day, it is filled in where it is; otherwise the number is added at the end of the day as a measurement, with source: naming the file.
  • A day that already has that number is left alone, so importing the same file twice adds nothing.
  • Several rows on one day (steps by the hour) are added up in the workspace. On the command line or in VS Code you can choose to average them instead (heart rate), or keep the last.
  • Dates like 2026-10-26, 2026/10/26 and 2026-10-26 07:30 always work. A date like 03/04/2026 could be either way round, so it is left out and counted; on the command line, --day-first reads it as the 3rd of April.

The numbers then chart like any others: see Numbers and charts.

The jot command line

cli/jot.mjs in the Jot project (Node 20 or later) does the same things from a terminal, so scripts, scheduled jobs and Apple Shortcuts can use them:

jot tasks journal.jot --status open          # today's to-do list, anywhere
jot events journal.jot --since 2026-10-01
jot numbers journal.jot                      # CSV
jot ics journal.jot -o ~/Calendars/jot.ics   # a calendar file
jot import fit.csv --into journal.jot        # numbers in, into their days
jot today journal.jot                        # today's entry
jot rollover journal.jot                     # carry open tasks to today
jot review journal.jot                       # this week's review
jot json journal.jot                         # everything, as JSON

The reading commands never change a file. The writing commands say what they changed, and --dry-run prints the result instead of saving it. jot help lists every option.

In VS Code

The Jot extension has the same commands (press Ctrl+Shift+P and type "Jot"): Today's Entry (Ctrl+Alt+T), Carry Open Tasks to Today, Add a Week Review, Export Calendar (.ics), Export as CSV and Import Numbers from CSV. Each change is one edit, so Undo takes it back.

To keep your calendar up to date without thinking about it, set jot.automation.exportOnSave.ics to a file in a folder that syncs (iCloud Drive, Dropbox, Google Drive, a web folder). Every time you save, the calendar file is written again, and a calendar app that subscribes to that file sees your journal's events.

Connecting to other services

These reach the internet, so each one only runs when you ask:

Connection How What is sent
Webhooks (Zapier, Make, n8n, IFTTT, your own) jot post <address> journal.jot, or Jot: Send to Webhook in VS Code (it asks first) the tasks, events and numbers as JSON: never the rest of your writing
Todoist jot todoist journal.jot with your API token in TODOIST_TOKEN, or Jot: Send Open Tasks to Todoist (the token is kept in VS Code's secret storage) each open task's text, due date and priority
Weather (Open-Meteo, no account) jot today journal.jot --weather 51.5,-0.12, or turn on jot.automation.weather.onToday with your location your latitude and longitude, rounded to about a kilometre

A webhook is the widest door: Zapier, Make and n8n turn it into thousands of services (a spreadsheet row per day, a message when a task is high priority, a note in another app). What arrives looks like this:

{ "format": "jot-automation", "version": 1, "file": "journal.jot",
  "tasks": [{ "text": "Post the letter", "status": "open", "priority": "normal", "date": "2026-10-28", "key": "…" }],
  "events": [{ "text": "Dentist 09:30", "date": "2026-10-28", "time": "09:30" }],
  "numbers": [{ "date": "2026-10-28", "metric": "steps", "value": 8200, "unit": "" }] }

Todoist gets each open task once. Jot remembers which tasks it has sent in a small record at the end of the journal (:::record sync #sync-todoist), so sending again only sends new ones. Formatted pages don't show this record.

The weather is written as a record, and its numbers chart like any others:

:::record observation #weather-2026-10-28
label: weather
sky: light rain
temperature-high: 14.3
temperature-low: 6.1
rain: 2.3
source: open-meteo.com
:::

Ideas

  • A scheduled job each morning (cron, Task Scheduler, a Shortcuts automation) running jot rollover and jot today, so the day starts with yesterday's open tasks waiting.
  • jot tasks journal.jot --status open --json in a Shortcut that shows your list on your phone's home screen.
  • A webhook to a Zapier zap that adds a spreadsheet row with each day's numbers.
  • Export on save to a calendar file your partner subscribes to, for shared plans.
